tools.image-denoise.faqs.0.question: How does denoising work?
tools.image-denoise.faqs.0.answer: The tool uses a median filter algorithm: for each pixel, it takes the median value of its surrounding neighborhood as the new value. This effectively removes random noise and salt-and-pepper noise while preserving edges better than a mean blur.
tools.image-denoise.faqs.1.question: What is noise?
tools.image-denoise.faqs.1.answer: Noise is the randomly distributed grain or colored speckles in a photo, usually caused by high ISO, low-light conditions, or JPEG compression. Denoising can dramatically improve the quality of such photos.
tools.image-denoise.faqs.2.question: Will denoising make my image blurry?
tools.image-denoise.faqs.2.answer: A median filter preserves edges better than blur-based algorithms, but overly strong denoising can still lose some detail. Start with a small radius and increase it gradually if you are not satisfied.
tools.image-denoise.faqs.3.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?

tools.image-deblur.faqs.0.question: How does deblurring work?
tools.image-deblur.faqs.0.answer: The tool uses Laplacian sharpening convolution: it detects edges (high-frequency detail) in the image and re-adds that detail on top of the image. Multiple iterations gradually enhance clarity.
tools.image-deblur.faqs.1.question: Can it fix severely blurred photos?
tools.image-deblur.faqs.1.answer: It works well for mild to moderate blur and out-of-focus shots, but detail lost in heavily blurred photos cannot be recovered out of thin air. Start with a low strength to avoid halos and noise.
tools.image-deblur.faqs.2.question: How should I set the parameters?
tools.image-deblur.faqs.2.answer: Strength controls how much sharpening is applied per iteration (20–50% is recommended), and iterations controls how many rounds are applied (1–3 is recommended). Too much strength produces a halo effect.

tools.unsharp-mask.faqs.0.question: What is an unsharp mask?
tools.unsharp-mask.faqs.0.answer: Unsharp Mask is the most classic sharpening algorithm in photography: it applies a Gaussian blur to the image, subtracts the blurred version from the original to get a detail mask, then blends the mask back in by a set ratio. It gives precise control over the sharpening amount and radius.
tools.unsharp-mask.faqs.1.question: What is the difference between amount and radius?
tools.unsharp-mask.faqs.1.answer: Amount controls the sharpening intensity, i.e. how much of the detail mask is blended in; Radius controls the sharpening range, i.e. the size of the blur kernel used when detecting detail. Small radii enhance fine edges, while large radii affect wider edge regions.
tools.unsharp-mask.faqs.2.question: Does sharpening damage image quality?
tools.unsharp-mask.faqs.2.answer: Moderate sharpening makes photos look crisper, but too much amount produces white halos and noise that look unnatural. Try starting with an amount of 60–100%.
tools.unsharp-mask.faqs.3.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?

tools.white-balance.faqs.0.question: What is white balance?
tools.white-balance.faqs.0.answer: White balance is the process of removing color casts from photos. Different light sources have different color temperatures, which can make photos look yellowish, bluish, or greenish. White balance correction makes white objects appear white in the photo.
tools.white-balance.faqs.1.question: How does the tool correct it?
tools.white-balance.faqs.1.answer: The tool uses the gray-world algorithm: it computes the average of the red, green, and blue channels across the whole image, then adjusts the channel gains so the three averages converge, neutralizing the color cast.
tools.white-balance.faqs.2.question: Which photos is it good for?
tools.white-balance.faqs.2.answer: It works well for photos taken under indoor incandescent (yellowish) or fluorescent (greenish) lighting, as well as photos with obvious color casts from sunsets or overcast days.
tools.white-balance.faqs.3.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
tools.white-balance.faqs.3.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

tools.auto-contrast.metadata.title: Auto Contrast - Optimize Photo Depth Online
tools.auto-contrast.metadata.description: Free online auto contrast tool. Histogram stretching automatically optimizes the light and dark distribution with an adjustable clip ratio, processed entirely in your browser.
tools.auto-contrast.title: Auto Contrast
tools.auto-contrast.description: Optimize your photo's contrast and dynamic range in one click. The tool analyzes the image histogram, automatically stretches the light and dark distribution, and lets you clip extreme pixels to avoid blown-out highlights and crushed shadows. All processing happens locally in your browser.
tools.auto-contrast.faqs.0.question: How does auto contrast work?
tools.auto-contrast.faqs.0.answer: The tool analyzes the image's brightness histogram, finds the actual darkest and brightest pixels, and stretches them across the full range (0–255), making the light and dark distribution fuller and giving the image more depth.
tools.auto-contrast.faqs.1.question: What does the clip ratio mean?
tools.auto-contrast.faqs.1.answer: The clip ratio decides how many extreme pixels are ignored. Setting it to 0.5% ignores the darkest and brightest 0.5% of pixels, preventing a few outliers (like specular highlights) from skewing the stretch.
tools.auto-contrast.faqs.2.question: Will it over-process my photo?
tools.auto-contrast.faqs.2.answer: The default 0.5% clip ratio is fairly gentle. If the image already has normal contrast, the stretch is minimal; low-contrast images see a clear improvement.
tools.auto-contrast.faqs.3.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
tools.auto-contrast.faqs.3.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

tools.histogram-equalize.metadata.title: Histogram Equalization - Boost Image Contrast Online
tools.histogram-equalize.metadata.descri: Free online histogram equalization tool. Redistributes pixel brightness to bring out detail in shadows and highlights, processed entirely in your browser.
tools.histogram-equalize.title: Histogram Equalization
tools.histogram-equalize.description: Apply the histogram equalization algorithm to redistribute the brightness distribution of the image's pixels, stretching contrast in the luminance domain so that detail in both shadows and highlights becomes more visible. Adjustable strength, processed entirely locally in your browser.
tools.histogram-equalize.faqs.0.question: What is histogram equalization?
tools.histogram-equalize.faqs.0.answer: Histogram equalization remaps pixel brightness so the image's brightness histogram is more evenly distributed. It spreads brightness concentrated in a narrow range across the full range, significantly boosting contrast.
tools.histogram-equalize.faqs.1.question: How is it different from auto contrast?
tools.histogram-equalize.faqs.1.answer: Auto contrast only does a linear stretch, while equalization performs a non-linear mapping based on the cumulative distribution function. It uses the full brightness range more thoroughly and is especially good at enhancing detail in low-contrast images.
tools.histogram-equalize.faqs.2.question: Will it introduce color casts?
tools.histogram-equalize.faqs.2.answer: The tool equalizes the luminance (grayscale) channel while keeping each pixel's color proportions unchanged, so it will not introduce color casts.
tools.histogram-equalize.faqs.3.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
tools.histogram-equalize.faqs.3.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

tools.histogram-equalize.guide.whatIs.bo: Histogram equalization is a classic image enhancement algorithm. It redistributes pixel brightness to make the histogram more uniform, boosting overall contrast.
It is ideal for backlit, underexposed, or hazy photos, bringing hidden detail to light.
tools.histogram-equalize.guide.howTo.ite: Drop or upload the photo you want to enhance.

tools.histogram-equalize.guide.tips.item: Works best on low-contrast, hazy photos.
A strength around 50% gives a more natural look.
Noise may become more visible after processing — pair with Image Denoise if needed.
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.metadata.title: HDR Tone Mapping - Reveal High Dynamic Range Online
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.metadata.descript: Free online HDR tone mapping tool. The Reinhard operator reveals highlight and shadow detail with adjustable exposure and strength, processed entirely in your browser.
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.title: HDR Tone Mapping
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.description: Apply the HDR tone mapping algorithm (Reinhard operator) to compress the light and dark differences of high-dynamic-range scenes, keeping highlights from blowing out and shadows full of detail. Adjustable exposure and strength, processed entirely locally in your browser.
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.faqs.0.question: What is HDR tone mapping?
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.faqs.0.answer: Tone mapping compresses the light and dark information of a high-dynamic-range (HDR) scene into a range that ordinary displays can show. The Reinhard operator applies non-linear compression to luminance, preserving detail in both highlights and shadows.
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.faqs.1.question: Does it work on ordinary photos?
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.faqs.1.answer: Yes. Even on a regular JPG, applying tone mapping makes highlights softer and shadow detail richer, producing an HDR-like look.
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.faqs.2.question: How should I understand the exposure parameter?
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.faqs.2.answer: Exposure mimics the exposure compensation used in HDR merging: raising it brightens shadows, while lowering it makes highlights more delicate. The default of 100% is neutral.
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.faqs.3.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.faqs.3.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.upload.drop: Drop a photo or click to upload
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.guide.whatIs.titl: What Is the HDR Tone Mapping Tool?
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.guide.whatIs.body: The HDR Tone Mapping tool uses the Reinhard operator to compress the image's luminance range, simulating the look of high-dynamic-range photography.
It makes highlights softer and shadow detail richer — ideal for backlit landscapes, night lights, and other scenes with a wide tonal range.
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.guide.howTo.title: How to Apply HDR Tone Mapping
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.guide.howTo.items: Drop or upload the photo you want to process.

Download the processed image as a PNG file.
tools.hdr-tone-mapping.guide.tips.title: Tips
Backlit and night photos show the most dramatic improvement.
An exposure of 120–150% enhances shadow detail.
Too much strength makes the image look flat — keep it around 80–100%.
tools.dehaze.metadata.title: Dehaze - Remove Fog and Haze from Photos Online
tools.dehaze.metadata.description: Free online dehazing tool. The dark channel prior algorithm removes fog and haze to restore clear, crisp landscapes, processed entirely in your browser.
tools.dehaze.title: Dehaze
tools.dehaze.description: Remove fog, haze, and the low contrast they cause in your photos, restoring a clear and crisp scene. The tool uses the dark channel prior algorithm to estimate and compensate for atmospheric scattering. All processing happens locally in your browser.
tools.dehaze.faqs.0.question: How does dehazing work?
tools.dehaze.faqs.0.answer: The tool uses the dark channel prior algorithm: it estimates the atmospheric light in the image, uses the dark channel to estimate the haze density (transmission) of each region, then reverses the atmospheric scattering to restore a clear scene.
tools.dehaze.faqs.1.question: Which photos is it good for?
tools.dehaze.faqs.1.answer: It works well on photos taken on foggy, hazy, or humid days, hazy-looking shots, and lightly misted mountain landscapes.
tools.dehaze.faqs.2.question: What does the window size mean?
tools.dehaze.faqs.2.answer: The window size is the local neighborhood range used when computing the dark channel, and it determines how finely the haze density is estimated. Larger windows give smoother estimates; smaller windows keep more detail.
tools.dehaze.faqs.3.question: Is my photo uploaded anywhere?
tools.dehaze.faqs.3.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your photos never leave your device.

tools.image-rotate-flip.faqs.0.answer: Yes. Besides the 90° quick buttons, a slider from -180° to 180° lets you rotate your image to any angle.
tools.image-rotate-flip.faqs.1.question: What's the difference between a horizontal flip and a vertical mirror?
tools.image-rotate-flip.faqs.1.answer: A horizontal flip mirrors the image left-to-right along the vertical axis (like a mirror), while a vertical mirror turns it upside down along the horizontal axis. The two can be combined.
tools.image-rotate-flip.faqs.2.question: Will rotation change the image size?
tools.image-rotate-flip.faqs.2.answer: Yes. When rotating at a custom angle, the output canvas expands to fit the rotated image, and the extra area is filled with a white background.

tools.image-negative.title: Negative/Invert
tools.image-negative.description: Invert every pixel color in your image (255 minus the original value) for a film negative look. Black-and-white photos take on an X-ray quality, while color photos produce interesting complementary-color effects. All processing happens locally in your browser.
tools.image-negative.faqs.0.question: What is the negative effect?
tools.image-negative.faqs.0.answer: The negative effect inverts every color in the image: black becomes white and white becomes black, with each color turning into its complementary color, just like a traditional film negative.
tools.image-negative.faqs.1.question: What is it good for?
tools.image-negative.faqs.1.answer: You can create X-ray-style black-and-white images, or give photos an artistic complementary-color look. Inverting again restores the original image.
tools.image-negative.faqs.2.question: Will I lose image information?
tools.image-negative.faqs.2.answer: No. Inversion is reversible — apply it again and the original colors come back.
tools.image-negative.faqs.3.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
tools.image-negative.faqs.3.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser — your image never leaves your device.
